content.text:
Top 5 recorded entries:

# Interactive daemon manager

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships `codegraph daemon` with alias `daemons` as an interactive manager for background daemons, showing the current project first and allowing stop-one or stop-all. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says this replaces hunting for a pid and killing it by hand.

# Rationale: Whole-file family skeletonization

Lifecycle status: accepted

Correcting the replacement record's graph shape: the current whole-file behavior should not be modeled as motivated by the proposed per-symbol future-work requirement; it is the current implementation limitation documented by this slice.

# Rationale: retract Anonymous handler link-through-body

Lifecycle status: accepted

Duplicate of existing Requirement "Arrow callback link-through" and existing ArchitecturalDecision "Arrow body link-through synthesis" from docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0; docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 restates the same anonymous-handler backlog rather than defining a distinct requirement.

# Project-name term exception

Lifecycle status: accepted

Project-name terms should be dropped from path scoring and explore type-disambiguation bias only when they are not the entire query; a bare project-name search must still work. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 search relevance bullet states the project name is dropped unless it is the only term.

# Declared return type requirement

Lifecycle status: accepted

The chained-call mechanism requires reliably declared factory return types to recover the receiver type. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Full README classification says the real requirement is a declared return type, not merely being statically typed, and that gradually typed or dynamic languages omit them too often.

# Rationale: Lua value-ref backlog

Lifecycle status: accepted

Corrected bootstrap edge shape: the validation invariant is a constraint and should constrain the proposed decision rather than be attached as an isMotivatedBy target.

Lifecycle status: accepted

Watch sync drops a single stale edge instead of aborting the whole daemon sync with a `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` error. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

# Streaming dynamic call linking

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph streams function and method records while linking dynamic call relationships instead of loading every function and method into memory at once. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says symbol-dense files with tens of thousands of functions or methods no longer exhaust the heap and memory stays flat no matter how many symbols the project has.

CodeGraph adoption work must optimize wall-clock time, tool-call count, and Read=0 rather than treating token cost as the primary target. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 states this doctrine constraint explicitly and notes token cost is lower as a side effect.

# Wording is low salience

Lifecycle status: accepted

Changing tool descriptions or server instructions alone is an unreliable way to move agent tool choice and has regressed wall-clock before. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 states this doctrine constraint and the clean A/B showed steering moved some tool choice but still left five Reads and no file-view use.

content.text:

# Watcher cost stays flat

Lifecycle status: accepted

The recursive and bounded watcher design keeps CodeGraph's background watch cost flat with project size and avoids machine-wide file-descriptor exhaustion. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says unrelated apps previously failed after the watcher piled up tens of thousands of handles, and the new strategy keeps cost flat regardless of project size.

# Flat-cost recursive watcher

Lifecycle status: accepted

The background watcher now uses a single recursive watch on macOS and Windows and bounded per-directory watches on Linux. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says this replaced one open file handle per watched file, keeping watcher cost flat no matter how large the project is.

# Shared project daemon

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph runs one background daemon per project shared by multiple AI agents, with one file watcher, one SQLite connection, and one tree-sitter warm-up instead of independent copies per client. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features.

Lifecycle status: accepted

The recursive and bounded watcher design keeps CodeGraph's background watch cost flat with project size and avoids machine-wide file-descriptor exhaustion. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says unrelated apps previously failed after the watcher piled up tens of thousands of handles, and the new strategy keeps cost flat regardless of project size.
